title: Tiered Workload Cost Template + Actionable Tuning Notes
summary: Working draft of a compact spreadsheet template and an associated set of prescriptive tuning notes designed for mixed-tier inference workloads. The focus is on capturing: per-route token economics, GPU-second pricing, TTL-based KV cache effectiveness, and quantization/batching tradeoffs for predictable reserved and burst usage.
purpose: Provide product, solutions, and SRE teams a one-page-cost-model spreadsheet they can copy and fill for a customer or a service to quickly recommend batching/caching/quantization presets and estimate monthly cost delta vs baseline.
audience: platform-eng, solutions-engineering, product managers evaluating Dedicated/Private pricing, and SREs running cost investigations
assumptions: 1) Token pricing and GPU-second rates are input cells maintained in the header. 2) Model families grouped (small, medium, large) with representative throughput and KV cache hit curves. 3) Baseline = single-token-per-request immediate response (no batching, no cache). 4) Workloads have two axes: steady-state QPS and episodic burst factor. 5) Latency SLO buckets: <50ms, 50-200ms, >200ms.
recommended_presets: Interactive low-latency (chat-like, SLO <50ms): small batch size 1-2, per-request KV cache TTL 30s, quantization: q4f16 for medium models, enable prefix-only cache, route to smallest model variant compatible with quality target.

Conversational session (multi-turn, medium latency acceptable 50-200ms): dynamic batching target 8-16 tokens per batch, KV cache TTL 10min for session prefix, leverage cached KV for repeated contexts, quantization: q4_0 for large models in Dedicated, conservative 8-bit asymmetric for Private deployments with validation.

High-throughput embedding/analysis (throughput prioritized): large batch sizes tuned by GPU memory (64-256 sequences), no per-request latency SLO, aggressive quantization (nf4/q8) with post-quantization quality checks, use route to Dedicated capacity with burst headroom.

Episodic burst (webhook spikes): keep baseline routing to hosted API with fallback to Dedicated if burst > x% of reserved; enable short TTL prefix cache (5s) to capture immediate repeats; pre-warm small dedicated instances for known campaign windows.
spreadsheet_instructions: Header: maintain cells for token_cost_per_1k, gpu_second_cost, avg_tokens_per_request, avg_generation_tokens, session_length_turns, burst_multiplier. Sections: (A) Baseline economics: compute tokens/month = QPS * avg_tokens * 3600 * 24 * 30. (B) Runtime profile: estimate GPU-seconds by mapping avg_tokens and batching efficiency to tokens/sec per GPU (lookup table in hidden sheet). (C) Cache impact: model hit-rate curve (TTL x session reuse) yields token_savings. (D) Quantization effect: quality risk multiplier and speedup factor. (E) Policy recommendation: choose preset row that matches SLO and desired unit-cost reduction. Use clearly labeled input cells (green) and outputs (blue). Include a sensitivity table that sweeps batch size and cache TTL to show delta cost and median latency impact.
example_metrics_and_cells:
EXAMPLE INPUTS:
- qps_peak: 120
- qps_steady: 10
- avg_tokens_in: 12
- avg_gen_tokens: 40
- token_cost_per_1k: $0.25
- gpu_second_cost: $0.035
CALCULATED OUTPUTS (example):
- tokens_month: 41,184,000
- baseline_monthly_token_cost: $10,296
- estimated_gpu_seconds_baseline: 18,000s -> gpu_cost: $630
- after_batching_and_qcache: token_cost -3%, gpu_seconds -40% -> total delta -26%
Notes: keep formula comments in adjacent column for reviewers; do not hardcode rates into formulas—reference header cells.
experiment_plan: 1) Copy template and populate with real traffic sample (7-day trace) for a target route. 2) Run three experiments in staging: A) batching only (increase batch target incrementally), B) TTL-only (increase TTL to measured reuse), C) quant-only (apply q4f16 or q8). 3) Measure cost, median latency, p95 latency, and delta in output token quality (via automated eval set). 4) Combine top-2 levers and validate regressions. 5) Produce a one-pager with recommended preset and expected unit economics for production rollout.
decision_log:
2025-11-10: Chose compact template over large multi-tab model to encourage adoption (Aisha).
2025-12-03: Agreed to include a hidden lookup sheet for tokens/sec per GPU by model family (Marco).
2026-01-21: Added conservative quality multiplier field to account for post-quantization checks (Chen).
2026-02-15: Updated example metrics to reflect new token pricing guidance (Riley).
open_questions: What is the canonical source of token_cost_per_1k and gpu_second_cost for Dedicated contracts?
Should we bake in a per-customer risk discount for aggressive quantization presets?
How to surface model-variant fallback economics when a route spans multiple model versions?
Can solutions-engineering add a small sample 7-day trace to the template for the onboarding runbook?
next_steps: - Get feedback from 2 solutions-eng pilots by 2026-03-01. - Add a lightweight script that can auto-populate the template from a 7-day JSON trace (follow-up GH PR). - Finalize a decision matrix that maps SLO + cost target -> preset and publish as product Optimize playbook entry.
notes_to_self: Keep the template small: users often abandon complex multi-tab sheets. Track adoption metrics: #copies, #linked_jira tickets. Consider exporting a read-only CSV variant suitable for embedding in proposal emails.
